why: A compact reference for the older but still useful immersive-agency shell: black-screen loader, progress bar, JS bootstrapping, and a positioning stack that explicitly spans motion, audio, 3D, and interactive graphics.

compositions.title: Progress bar landing shell
compositions.study: The first visible layer is a full-screen loader with a dedicated progress bar before the runtime is attached.
compositions.reuse: Use when the experience benefits from a deliberate prelude instead of jumping straight into content.

compositions.title: Black-canvas base layer
compositions.study: The shell sets a black background and defers the interactive experience to a JS loader rather than laying out a normal DOM-first homepage.
compositions.reuse: Use for immersive portfolios or studio sites where motion direction should own the first impression.

assets.notes: The page metadata and shell language point to a media system that mixes video with interactive graphics.
assets.reuse: Plan media as a native part of the experience instead of one disconnected hero clip.

assets.notes: Progress bars and browser-support messaging are treated as first-class visual layers.
assets.reuse: Keep boot, wait, and failure states visually aligned with the main stage.

motion.title: Progress-led boot sequence
motion.notes: The shell exposes `loader__` elements plus a foreground progress bar to pace entry into the experience.
motion.fallback: Old-browser messaging exists, but reduced-motion behavior was not visible from static inspection.

motion.title: Runtime-owned motion narrative
motion.notes: Because RequireJS loads the actual experience, the motion system likely owns its own chaptering rather than relying on default document scroll.
motion.fallback: Needs live browser review before treating the exact chapter model as reusable guidance.

interactions.title: Boot-gated interaction model
interactions.study: The interactive experience is explicitly gated behind the runtime loader instead of exposing plain content immediately.
interactions.reuse: Use when navigation and interaction should feel like part of one audiovisual world.

interactions.title: Capability-checked stage entry
interactions.study: The shell ships a compatibility branch for old browsers and then hands off to JS, which makes capability checks part of the interaction contract.
interactions.reuse: Treat capability gates as a visible part of immersive design rather than a silent crash path.

implementation.format: black-background loader shell with RequireJS runtime boot
implementation.notes: Static inspection confirmed full-screen loader elements, progress bars, compatibility messaging, and a runtime-loaded interactive layer; deeper scene behavior still needs backfill.
